title: Challenge the local-flow assumption
brief: Audit the freestream-equals-local-flow assumption. Use explicit teaching factors to see how a favorable baseline can lose margin.
supplied: Can the freestream-based trainer authority estimate be reused when the elevator sees slower local flow?
M_baseline=0.5*rho*V²*S*c*dCm; M_local=0.5*rho*(flowFactor*V)²*S*c*dCm. Required control moment remains 1350 N m.

900 kg trainer; rho=1.20 kg/m³; V=20 m/s; S=27.25 m²; c=4 m; usable dCm=0.153; Iy=5000 kg m²; other=-750 N m; target=0.12 rad/s². Nose-up moment is positive about the declared CG. Teaching sensitivity parameter flowFactor=0.7; it is not a measured tail-flow value.
Freestream-based capacity, local-flow sensitivity capacity, and whether each exceeds 1350 N m.
This factor study isolates speed sensitivity; real local flow may also change the usable coefficient. It does not independently validate tail aerodynamics.
A 0.7 local-speed factor gives 0.49 of the baseline capacity. A 0.5 factor may remove sufficient authority.
At 0.7: available=1961.2152 N m and margin=611.2152 N m. At 0.5: available=1000.62 N m and margin=-349.38 N m.
Compare factors 1, 0.7 and 0.5 with unchanged density, geometry, usable coefficient and moment demand.
Label the factor as a teaching assumption. Show baseline, adjusted capacity, demand and limitations.
At each flowFactor evaluate the two equations above; preserve the declared configuration and required moment.
Request local-flow and coefficient evidence at the limiting alpha, flap/power state and loading; do not claim the freestream estimate is universally valid.

fields.label: What does the original estimate assume about airflow at the elevator?
options: It assumes airflow at the elevator has the same speed as the undisturbed airflow.
Control moment is independent of speed
fields.help: The original estimate uses the aircraft flight speed to calculate elevator authority. Identify the assumption this makes; you are not being asked whether it is always true. The wing wake or propeller flow can change the local airspeed.

fields.label: With slower air at the elevator, is the original estimate too high or too low?
fields.help: If the air at the elevator is slower than assumed, does the original calculation predict too much or too little available moment? Hold the coefficient fixed.

optionLabels.Overestimates available authority: Predicts more available moment than this model gives
optionLabels.Underestimates available authority: Predicts less available moment than this model gives
optionLabels.Proves the tail is valid: Proves the elevator model is accurate

fields.label: Adjusted capacity ÷ original capacity at 70% local speed
fields.help: Enter adjusted capacity divided by original capacity when local speed is 0.7 times flight speed. Enter a fraction such as 0.25, not a percentage. Enter a number only.

fields.label: Explain your answer
fields.help: Explain which airflow assumption the original estimate makes and how a lower local speed changes the estimate when the coefficient stays fixed.

checks.expected: It assumes airflow at the elevator has the same speed as the undisturbed airflow.
checks.message: The original estimate substitutes flight speed for local elevator airspeed. This is a modeling assumption, not a verified fact about the aircraft.
Slower local flow reduces this held-coefficient moment estimate.
Square the local-speed ratio while holding other terms fixed.

hints: The speed entering the coefficient model must match the airflow and control-surface data.
Moment scales with speed squared only while the other terms remain fixed.
0.7²=0.49. Propwash may help and wake/separation may hurt; neither is validated by this factor study.

sweep.units: Local speed factor dimensionless; available and required moment in N m.

experience.scenario: The trainer may encounter local airflow at its elevator slower than the freestream used in the original estimate. This is a teaching sensitivity study, not measured tail-flow data.
experience.task: Identify the original airflow assumption. Predict whether slower air at the elevator makes the original estimate too high or too low. Calculate adjusted capacity divided by original capacity for a local-speed factor of 0.7.
experience.method: flowFactor = local speed / freestream speed. A factor of 0.7 means 70% speed. With all other quantities held fixed, capacity scales with the square of that fraction. Your assumption answers are checked against the supplied sensitivity model; they do not alter that model.
experience.investigate: Compare factors 1, 0.7 and 0.5 with demand held fixed. When does the original sufficient-authority claim fail?
experience.tools: Only this app and its calculation pad are needed.

reflection.included: The experiment changes local speed at the control surface while holding the usable coefficient increment fixed.
reflection.omitted: It does not model how disturbed flow might also change control effectiveness.
reflection.question: If disturbed flow changes both local speed and control effectiveness, what additional evidence would you need to revise the available-moment estimate?
reflection.help: Use one specific detail from this investigation. Explain what you would check next and why it matters; you do not need to perform that new test here.

experience.terms: Freestream means airflow away from the aircraft disturbances. Local flow is the air reaching the elevator. The local-speed factor is local speed divided by freestream speed. In this exercise the coefficient stays fixed while speed changes.
